chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 325: A Man-Monster Battle of Flesh and Tentacles
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang is trapped by Renxiao and forced to tear himself in half. With tentacles for legs and a sword in hand, he turns his own body into a weapon in a desperate fight for survival.
og_title: A Body Split in Two, Tentacles for Legs
og_description: The Dao-Twisted World's horror reaches a new peak as Li Huowang’s fight for survival forces him to become a literal monster.
twitter_description: Li Huowang’s desperate gambit goes horribly right, leaving him a writhing mass of flesh, tentacles, and pure spite.

lore_anchors.definition: In the Dao-Twisted World, blind, malformed creatures created from humans who suffer into extreme old age, their bodies twisting into hollow parodies of life.
A traditional Chinese heavy pole weapon with a curved blade, famously associated with the god of war Guan Yu.
A classic Daoist exorcism tool, believed to be effective against malevolent spirits and walking dead.
A ritual weapon made of old Chinese coins strung on red thread, used for exorcism and containing potent spiritual energy.
A primordial, pain-feeding god worshipped by the Ao-Jing Sect; its power is accessed through self-mutilation and sacrifice.
A grotesque, parasitic entity inside Li Huowang that suppresses his hallucinations and can be controlled as a physical weapon.
